themes_detail.label: Explosive Graffiti Spike
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 30 THIS WEEK—a 1233% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 2.2 per week—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapid deterioration of property maintenance in Elmhurst/South Corona.
evidence: 30 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 25.47)
1233% spike represents most statistically extreme anomaly in dataset
Temporal clustering suggests event-driven cause rather than ambient trend
reporting_angles: On-the-ground visual survey: document locations, styles, and tags to identify organized crew vs. copycat activity
Interview Parks Dept, NYPD, local business owners on enforcement response and known groups active in corridor

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 16 THIS WEEK—an 700% increase from the 2.0 weekly baseline—indicating possible organized events, unsupervised gatherings, or new loud activities in district parks during warm weather.
evidence: 16 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 8.85)
700% spike concentrated in single week suggests acute trigger, not gradual shift
Aligns with seasonal pattern but magnitude far exceeds normal variation
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints; check for permitted events, scheduled concerts, or construction
Resident interviews: which times of day, what type of noise, how long has it persisted?

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints hit 4 THIS WEEK—a 540% spike from the 0.6 weekly baseline—suggesting new or recently problematic retail locations or consumer behavior issues in Elmhurst/South Corona.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.85)
540% spike reflects new phenomenon; prior 8-week baseline suggests few or no legal retailers in district
Timing suggests either new store openings or recent enforcement/compliance issues at existing locations
reporting_angles: Map licensed dispensaries in CD 404; cross-reference complaint addresses to determine if complaints target legal operators or unlicensed sellers
Interview residents on nature of complaints: loitering, odor, sales to minors, public consumption, etc.

themes_detail.label: Tree/Vegetation Management Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 9 THIS WEEK—a 454% spike from the 1.6 weekly baseline—pointing to inadequate Parks Dept maintenance or storm damage in the district.
evidence: 9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 8.61)
454% spike concentrated in single week suggests acute trigger: recent weather event, end of seasonal hiring, or response to backlog
Converges with long-standing CB budget request for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity'
reporting_angles: Check Parks Dept work orders for CD 404; identify any recent staffing changes or weather impacts
Visual canvass of streets and parks to document hazards from overgrown trees (visibility, pedestrian/vehicle risk)

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Service Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker and vehicle complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK—a 967% increase from the 0.4 weekly baseline—signaling potential service failures, uncollected trash, or street cleaning gaps in specific neighborhoods.
evidence: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
967% spike is rare event; prior 8-week baseline shows virtually no complaints of this type
Suggests either operational change (route closure, vehicle breakdown, staff absence) or organized resident complaint campaign
reporting_angles: DSNY records: are any sanitation routes missing scheduled pickups or sweeps this week in CD 404?
Resident interviews: what specific sanitation failures are being reported (missed collections, broken equipment, vehicle collisions)?
